briefs.brief: The lead vehicle in the ego lane is already stopped; the ego closes on it and must avoid a rear-end.
The lead vehicle brakes hard in flowing traffic; the ego follows at a normal headway with a human reaction delay.
The lead vehicle brake-checks the ego briefly then resumes.
The ego arrives at the tail of a stopped queue at speed.
Stop-and-go traffic: the lead repeatedly stops and moves off.
The ego is tailgated while the lead ahead brakes.
A vehicle cuts in close ahead of the ego then brakes.
A lead vehicle cuts out and reveals a stopped vehicle ahead.
A vehicle pulls out of a parking space directly into the ego lane.
A merging vehicle takes a gap that collapses.
The ego lane drops and traffic must merge late.
A vehicle drifts from the adjacent lane into the ego blind spot.
The ego turns left across an oncoming through vehicle at a junction.
Cross traffic runs the stop control into the ego path at a junction.
A vehicle enters the junction late against the signal.
The ego turns right across a cyclist continuing straight.
At an uncontrolled junction a vehicle emerges from behind an obstruction.
Two vehicles negotiate an all-way stop and both proceed.
A child runs into the road from between two parked vehicles.
An adult crosses mid-block into the ego path.
A pedestrian steps out from behind a stopped vehicle in the adjacent lane.
A pedestrian emerges in front of a stopped bus.
A pedestrian starts crossing, hesitates, then continues.
A pedestrian crosses from the far side into the ego path.
A cyclist crosses the ego path from the nearside.
A parked car door opens into a cyclist who swerves into the ego lane.
A cyclist rides against traffic toward the ego.
A motorcycle filters between lanes past the ego.
A lane-closure taper forces traffic to merge in front of the ego.
A single-lane work zone with a flagger controls alternating one-way flow.
A work zone shifts the alignment laterally and the ego steers around it.
A road worker steps out of the work area into the live lane.
Construction occupies part of an intersection with plant, barriers and a flagger.
A disabled vehicle is stopped in the ego lane.
Debris lies in the ego lane.
An animal crosses into the ego path.
A hazard sits just beyond a crest or curve.
An oncoming vehicle encroaches over the centreline on a bend.
A wrong-way vehicle approaches the ego head-on.
A third party overtakes toward the ego in the oncoming lane.
A vehicle backs out of a parking space into the ego path.
A vehicle emerges from a driveway into the ego path.
A double-parked delivery vehicle blocks the ego lane.
A ball rolls out followed by a child in a school zone.
A crossing guard releases children across the ego path.
Chaotic school drop-off with vehicles and children.
The ego faces a yellow-light dilemma zone at a signal.
Temporary signals or an officer override the normal control.
A vehicle ahead brakes for nothing (phantom-brake bait).
A truck ahead sheds part of its load.
A vehicle already circulating conflicts with the ego entering a roundabout.
A circulating vehicle cuts across the ego exit path.
A vehicle emerges from behind a row of parked cars.
A pedestrian steps out from behind a double-parked truck.
A stopped bus hides a cyclist from the ego.
A roadside hedge hides a crossing pedestrian at a corner.
A queue in the adjacent lane hides a crossing pedestrian.
A crest hides a stopped vehicle from the ego.
A vehicle ahead loses traction on a friction patch.
A third-party vehicle spins into the ego path.
A slower lead vehicle is encountered at closing speed (Euro NCAP CCRm).
The ego crests a rise into the tail of a stopped queue.
Two vehicles weave across each other around the ego.
A vehicle merges from an on-ramp into the ego lane.
A vehicle crosses the ego lane to reach an exit.
The ego turns left across traffic approaching from the left.
Straight crossing paths conflict at an uncontrolled junction.
The ego turns left across an oncoming motorcycle.
The ego is caught in the dilemma zone as the signal changes.
An emergency vehicle crosses the junction against the ego.
A pedestrian crosses from the nearside close to the ego (NCAP CPNA).
A pedestrian crosses from the far side (NCAP CPFA).
A pedestrian walks behind a reversing vehicle.
A group of pedestrians crosses together.
A cyclist crosses from the nearside close to the ego (NCAP CBNA).
A cyclist is right-hooked by a turning vehicle ahead of the ego.
An e-scooter enters the ego lane from the footway.
A slow-moving work vehicle occupies the ego lane.
Barriers narrow the ego lane through a work area.
A night work zone with limited conspicuity.
An accident scene partially blocks the ego lane.
Fallen cargo blocks part of the ego lane.
Two vehicles negotiate a narrow road with limited width.
The ego judges a gap to overtake with oncoming traffic.
Two vehicles contest the same parking space.
A conflict occurs in a parking aisle at low speed.
A school bus deploys its stop arm and children cross.
A signal outage leaves the junction flashing.
A rail crossing activates as the ego approaches.
A convoy of vehicles prevents the ego from merging.
Pedestrians occupy the carriageway unexpectedly.
A pedestrian stands at the kerb but does not cross (negative control).

split.policy: DEV briefs may be used to develop and debug the TOOL SURFACE. HELDOUT briefs are never inspected while iterating; they are authored once through the frozen, unmodified surface. The reported number is the generalization gap in admission rate.
